prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: advisory WUI wildfire decision support. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (alias Emberhall): primary interface; opens triage case when automated confidence exceeds threshold; records reason per triage decision (advanced/held/dismissed); marks radio route impaired on bridge failure, requiring Orion manual acknowledgement; jurisdictional constraints entered before Drone Pilot Operator route briefing. North/South Lookout Camera Masts: hardened power, lightning protection, licensed wireless video, cellular fallback; smoke-visibility context for Air Attack Supervisor; North sends Thermal Spot Snippet; South produces Camera Cleaning Log. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (alias Kestrel): produces Battery Swap Ticket. Drone Tasking Service: flight requests, constraints, status; not flight-release authority; may prepare Kestrel verification task when fixed view blocked; shall not issue launch conflicting with active aviation lane in Marigold. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (alias Lantern): common event record; traceable recommendations; retains timing, source IDs, model versions, acknowledgments; score not fire declaration; supplies perimeter intelligence. Smoke Classifier Module: sends plume confidence to Lantern; produces Ridge Shadow Mask. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (alias Brindle): wind/visibility context; sends Wind Shift Bulletin. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (alias Badger): recorded, access-controlled; bridges command, air-to-ground, county paths; shall preserve source speaker identity. Crewline Mobile Tablet: Helitack Crew Leader receives only confirmed released context. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (alias Marigold): aviation lanes/status. East/West Retardant Loading Pumps: East sends Retardant Batch Slip after load metered and sealed. Actors: County Emergency Liaison: county dispatch, roads, evacuation; sends Drone Corridor Permit after jurisdiction review. Duty Detection Officer (alias Orion): reviews triage, records restriction basis; must verify alternate contact for impaired route before accepting aviation messages. Air Attack Supervisor (alias Redtail): confirms operating window; deconflicts routes before drone launch; checks restrictions against Lantern perimeter before releasing air assets. Tanker Base Manager: sequences tankers via Marigold; confirms pump readiness before tanker assignment. Drone Pilot Operator: confirms task safe. States: suspected ignition (held if evidence inconsistent, stale, or single low-confidence source); Confirmed Ignition State needs persistent smoke/thermal cue plus independent sensor, field report, or recorded authorized human judgment; enables suppression planning. Airspace Restricted State: only after TFR accepted by responsible

New part:
S096: The Smoke Classifier Module may be temporarily down-weighted by the Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine when observation quality is suspected to be degraded.
S097: The Helitack Crew Leader uses the Crewline Mobile Tablet to acknowledge air-to-ground instructions and report whether crews are inside any planned drop or reconnaissance area.
S098: The Caldera Incident Command Portal displays crew acknowledgements beside aviation tasks so the Air Attack Supervisor can verify that ground resources are clear before authorizing flight activity.
S099: If the Confirmed Ignition State is active and airspace approval is delayed, the system keeps suppression planning visible while preventing premature aircraft dispatch.
S100: Coordination records are retained with timestamps, participant identities, and radio path status so post-incident review can reconstruct both aviation decisions and interagency notifications.
S101: This section defines how the system converts detection observations, aerial imagery, weather updates, and geospatial overlays into a shared fire behavior assessment for operational use.
S102: The assessment begins when visual detections are correlated with incident geometry, terrain, fuel type, and current resource locations in the mapping workspace.
S103: North Lookout Camera Mast captures a time-stamped smoke column bearing and reports the pan, tilt, zoom, and confidence values needed to project the observation onto terrain.
S104: South Lookout Camera Mast supplies a separate bearing track so the mapping workflow can triangulate a probable origin area and bound the uncertainty ellipse.
S105: The Smoke Classifier Module assigns each observation a smoke likelihood, growth trend, and obscuration flag before the result is made available for analyst review.
S106: The Duty Detection Officer uses the spot snippet to compare the automated classification with visible flame, smoke color, and terrain context before accepting the observation into the assessment queue.
S107: Drone imagery is treated as a higher-resolution confirmation layer when weather, airspace, and communications conditions permit flight operations.
S108: The Drone Tasking Service packages approved imaging objectives as map footprints, altitude bands, and revisit intervals so the requested coverage can be compared with the active perimeter model.
S109: The Drone Pilot Operator uses the swap ticket to keep imaging sorties aligned with available aircraft endurance and expected return time.
S110: Frames collected during a sortie are orthorectified against the terrain model and registered to the incident grid before they are used for perimeter adjustment.
S111: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine identifies heat signatures, smoke edges, flame fronts, and potential spot fire indicators in the registered imagery.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
